title.narrative: Multi-Sectoral Assistance for Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Rural Damascus

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project is framed in the plans and assumption of UNRWA’s “syria, lebanon and jordan emergency appeal 2024” (EA 2024) which advocates the minimum assistance needed to ameliorate the worst effects of the humanitarian crisis in Syria. The estimated 438.000 Palestine Refugees now living in Syria, who were already amongst the most vulnerable groups in the country, are continuously pushed further into vulnerability and poverty and remain highly dependent on the assistance provided by UNRWA to meet their basic needs. Under this project, UNRWA aims to maintain vulnerable Palestine Refugees’ access to (1) primary healthcare services and (2) food security in the SHF targeted areas of Babella, Dhameer, Qudsiya, and Duma, in Rural Damascus.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt(1) UNRWA's 6 health facilities (Qaber Essit, Sbeineh, Husieneih, Ramadan, Duma, Qudsiya) provide a range of primary health services, including out-patient consultations, immunization services, infant and child growth monitoring, dispensing of medications, gynecology consultations, laboratory services, non-communicable disease (NCD) care, maternal and child health care, dental and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services. 84,350 Palestine refugees that have access to primary health care in the targeted UNRWA health facilities will benefit from this activity through the funding of 36 frontline health staff salaries for 7-8 months. These staff include medical officers, nurses, medical clerks, midwives, medical laboratory technologists, and pharmacists working in different health centres. Under this project, UNRWA is requesting to cover the staff salary as other costs (drugs, running costs) are covered by other donors.lt/pgtltpgt(2) Under this project, UNRWA will provide food baskets for the 9,554 most vulnerable Palestine Refugees residing in the area. In order to ensure optimal utilization of the financial resources, UNRWA is targeting only the most vulnerable categories of Palestine refugees for this activity, including (a) families headed by a person older than 60 years old (b) families that include a person with disabilities (c) families headed by a female and (d) orphans. lt/pgtltpgtThis project contributed to UNRWA's in-kind food assistance under Emergency Appeal 2024 which aims to provide 155,000 most vulnerable Palestine Refugees with 12 months of in-kind food assistance. The actual coverage of months will depend on the availability of funds, and this project will cover part of the first round of in-kind food distribution in 2024 covering 3 months. This assistance is also designed to complement UNRWA's Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance, which will support the same population with six to eight months of cash assistance. ltspangtEach food basket for one person includes wheat flour, rice, pasta, bulgur wheat, white beans, vegetable oil, sugar, chickpeas, lentils, sardines, tomato paste and milk. The composition of the food basket was developed based on WFP guidelines except for milk. Milk is not for infants but for people of all ages, which is lt/spangtltspangtcrucial for children’s bone and dental health and helps prevent calcium deficiency and osteoporosis forlt/spangtltspangt the elderly and persons with disabilities. Accordingly it became lt/spangtltspangtpart of the UNRWA recommended dietary allowance for the targeted categories and part of UNRWA’s food baskets under 2024 Emergency Appeal, to which this project contributes. Wheat flour is included in the basket since 2021, following WFP guidelines. The quantity was reduced from 25 kg planned per person in 2021 to 5 kg per person, based on feedback received from beneficiaries. The quantities of the other items were adjusted to ensure sufficient nutritional value and to cover 50% of the daily calorie requirements per capita in compliance with Food and Agriculture sector guidance.lt/spangtlt/pgt
